correctness.rationale: Every ≥3-vertex general-position corona set uses at most one vertex from each core-pendant pair; the n exceptional same-root pairs are independently valid and counted as nz². Projecting a set with distinct selected roots U onto G, any selected internal geodesic root must be represented by its pendant, while each geodesically extreme root can independently choose core or pendant, giving 2^{e_G(U)}. For a tree the leaves of the minimal connected hull of U are exactly its extreme roots; for each connected subtree H≥2 all hull leaves must be selected (weight 2z) and internal vertices can be absent or represented by pendants (weight 1+z). The postorder F_v,R_v recurrence splits subtrees by unique topmost vertex without double counting. Leading coefficient 2^{s(G)} uses the characterization of simplicial vertices as never internally geodesic; cubic formula follows from the two possibilities for three roots. Independent checks compared the DP with a separately implemented root-subset projection on ten trees, supplementing a structural all-order proof.

value.rationale: The arbitrary-tree corona family is a natural exact extension of previously studied comb and complete-core special cases. The all-coefficient connected-subtree weight formula and polynomial-time rooted recursion give structural counting control for every tree, while a general connected-core root-extremality projection and simplicial leading coefficient are useful independent consequences. It explicitly leaves the separate unimodality problem unresolved.

final_claim: For any n≥3 tree T with one private leaf attached at each core vertex, the full general-position polynomial of T∘K1 has exact connected-subtree expansion with 2z per hull leaf and 1+z per internal vertex, computable by rooted DP. For connected simple G≥3 the general corona projection counts 2^{e_G(U)} per distinct-root subset, yielding 2^{s(G)} highest coefficient and exact cubic identity.
limitations: Applicable to n≥3 connected simple core graphs for general projection and n≥3 trees for polynomial-time DP; no claims of arbitrary-core polynomial-time algorithm.
Potential unindexed general transformation remains a priority risk.
